title: Solid State Ceiling and Wall Wash Lighting with Cabin Intercommunication Scene Control

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Lighting — Ceiling and Wall Wash Lights

abstract: Light-emitting diode strips with tunable colour temperature replace the fluorescent ceiling and wall wash lighting, driven from the cabin intercommunication system so that operators can define boarding, cruise and disembarkation scenes.

sections.reason: Two things came together. Fluorescent tubes for this application were going obsolete as the supplier consolidated its European lamp production, and operators refreshing their cabins were asking for the scene lighting they already had on their newer aircraft. The electronic ballast standard introduced earlier had solved the flicker complaint but had not changed the tube supply position and offered no colour control at all. A solid state answer closed both.
sections.description: The fluorescent tubes and their ballasts are replaced by light-emitting diode strips with independently driven warm and cool channels, mounted in the existing stowage envelope D3320117509271 and behind the same diffuser aperture. The curtain rail sub-assembly D3320000585452 carries the new driver, and the shear head bolts LN983579-8C are retained. The cargo lining latch D2550114658909 is included in the change because the same driver family feeds the cargo compartment lights, which are converted in the same operation. Colour scene control is provided by the cabin intercommunication database load LG9N7BD4A16, addressed through the director FIN 3RK. The wall wash lining FIN 9RH is unchanged and the cargo lining light FIN 3596DQ is converted to the new driver. Work is done in zones 265, 271, 291 and 131.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of 11.8 kg per aircraft. Electrical load falls by a further 640 VA at full output and by considerably more at the dimmed scenes. The strips are not interchangeable with the fluorescent standard because the driver interface and the dimming protocol differ, so a cabin zone must be converted in full. The database load must match the cabin layout, which means a per-operator configuration file rather than a single fleet standard. IPC and AMM content for ATA 33-20 and the cargo lighting content in ATA 25-50 required re-issue, and the cabin intercommunication configuration procedure was extended.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN Z11105 in May 2022. Retrofit is a two-night activity per aircraft including the database load and the scene definition, and is normally combined with a cabin refresh.

type_data.balance_impact: Distributed along the cabin, no measurable CG effect
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN Z11105; the fluorescent standard was withdrawn from the line at the same time
